title: The Decline of Insects
passage:
In 2017, a study in Germany reported that the total mass of flying insects in nature reserves had fallen by more than 75 percent over 27 years. The finding shocked scientists and the public, and similar declines have since been reported in many other parts of the world. Because insects pollinate crops, break down waste, and serve as food for birds and other animals, their decline could have serious consequences for entire ecosystems.

Researchers have identified several causes. The most important appears to be the loss of habitat, as natural areas are converted into farmland, roads, and buildings. Intensive agriculture also plays a role. Large fields of a single crop provide few flowers for insects to feed on, and pesticides can kill insects directly or weaken them. Climate change and light pollution, which confuses insects that are active at night, are also thought to contribute.

Measuring insect populations, however, is difficult. There are millions of species, many of which have never been studied, and long-term data exist for only a small number of places. Some scientists warn against assuming that all insects are declining everywhere at the same rate. In some areas, certain species have actually increased.

Despite these uncertainties, experts say that people can take simple steps to help. Farmers can leave strips of wildflowers along the edges of fields, and cities can reduce the mowing of grass in parks. Even individuals can make a difference by planting native flowers in their gardens and avoiding the use of pesticides. Researchers stress that because insects reproduce quickly, populations can often recover if their habitats are restored.
translation:
2017年、ドイツの研究で、自然保護区の飛翔昆虫の総量が27年間で75%以上減ったと報告された。この結果は科学者や一般の人々に衝撃を与え、その後世界の多くの地域で同様の減少が報告されている。昆虫は作物の受粉を助け、ごみを分解し、鳥などのえさになるため、その減少は生態系全体に深刻な影響を及ぼしうる。

研究者はいくつかの原因を挙げている。最も大きいのは、自然の土地が農地や道路や建物に変わることによる生息地の喪失のようだ。集約的な農業も関係している。単一の作物の広い畑には昆虫がえさにできる花が少なく、農薬は昆虫を直接殺したり弱らせたりする。気候変動や、夜に活動する昆虫を混乱させる光害も一因と考えられている。

しかし、昆虫の数を測るのは難しい。何百万もの種があり、その多くは研究されたことがなく、長期的なデータがある場所はごくわずかだ。すべての昆虫がどこでも同じ割合で減っていると決めつけないよう警告する科学者もいる。地域によっては、実際に増えている種もある。

こうした不確かさはあるものの、人々は簡単な方法で助けられると専門家は言う。農家は畑の端に野草の帯を残し、都市は公園の芝刈りを減らせる。個人でも、庭に在来の花を植え、農薬を使わないようにすることで違いを生み出せる。研究者は、昆虫は繁殖が速いので、生息地を回復すれば数が戻ることが多いと強調している。

questions.question: According to the passage, what appears to be the main cause of insect decline?
choices: The loss of natural habitats
Light pollution in cities
An increase in birds
Cold weather
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、最も大きい原因は生息地の喪失のようだとある。光害は一因として挙げられているだけ。

questions.question: Why do some scientists warn against making general conclusions?
choices: All insect species have been studied in detail.
The German study was proven to be wrong.
Insects are no longer important to ecosystems.
Data are limited, and some species have increased.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、長期データのある場所はわずかで、増えている種もあるとある。

questions.question: What do researchers stress in the final paragraph?
choices: Insect populations can recover if habitats are restored.
Only governments can help insects.
Pesticides are necessary to protect insects.
Insect populations will never recover.
questions.explanation: 昆虫は繁殖が速く、生息地を回復すれば数が戻ることが多いと強調している。個人でもできることがあるとも述べている。

title: Music and Memory
passage:
Many people have had the experience of hearing an old song and suddenly remembering a specific moment from their past. Scientists have long been interested in the strong connection between music and memory, and recent research suggests that this connection may help people with memory problems.

One reason music is so memorable is that it activates many different areas of the brain at the same time, including those involved in emotion, movement, and hearing. Memories linked to strong emotions are generally easier to recall, and music often accompanies emotional events such as weddings, graduations, and celebrations. Brain-imaging studies have also shown that some regions that process familiar music are relatively unaffected in the early stages of Alzheimer's disease.

This may explain why some patients with dementia who struggle to recognize family members can still sing the songs of their youth. Care homes in several countries have begun creating personalized playlists for residents based on the music they enjoyed when they were young. Staff report that listening to these songs can reduce anxiety and agitation and sometimes encourages patients to talk about their memories.

Researchers caution, however, that music is not a cure for dementia. The improvements in mood are often temporary, and music cannot reverse the damage that the disease causes to the brain. Nevertheless, because music programs are inexpensive and have few side effects, many experts believe they are a valuable addition to medical treatment, improving the quality of life for patients and their families.
translation:
昔の歌を聞いて、過去のある瞬間を突然思い出した経験がある人は多いだろう。科学者は長い間、音楽と記憶の強い結びつきに関心を持ってきた。最近の研究によれば、この結びつきは記憶に問題を抱える人の助けになるかもしれない。

音楽がこれほど記憶に残る理由の一つは、感情、動き、聴覚に関わる部分など、脳の多くの領域を同時に働かせることだ。強い感情と結びついた記憶はふつう思い出しやすく、音楽は結婚式、卒業式、祝いの席など感情が動く出来事に伴うことが多い。脳画像の研究でも、なじみのある音楽を処理する領域の一部は、アルツハイマー病の初期段階では比較的影響を受けにくいことがわかっている。

このことは、家族の顔もわからなくなった認知症の患者が、若いころの歌はまだ歌える理由を説明しているのかもしれない。いくつかの国の介護施設では、入居者が若いころに好きだった音楽をもとに、一人ひとりのプレイリストを作り始めている。職員によると、こうした歌を聞くと不安や興奮が和らぎ、患者が思い出を語り出すこともあるという。

しかし研究者は、音楽は認知症の治療法ではないと注意を促している。気分の改善は一時的なことが多く、病気が脳に与える損傷を元に戻すことはできない。それでも、音楽プログラムは費用が安く副作用もほとんどないため、多くの専門家は、患者と家族の生活の質を高める医療の貴重な補完になると考えている。

questions.question: Why might some dementia patients still be able to sing old songs?
choices: They practice singing every day.
Music cures the damage to their brains.
They have no memory problems at all.
Brain areas that process familiar music may be less affected by the disease.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、なじみのある音楽を処理する領域は初期段階で比較的影響を受けにくいとあり、第3段落がそれを受けている。

questions.question: What have care homes reported about personalized playlists?
choices: They make patients forget their families.
They can help reduce patients' anxiety.
They are too expensive to create.
They cause patients to become more agitated.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、不安や興奮が和らぎ、思い出を語り出すこともあると職員が報告している。

questions.question: What is the researchers' view of music programs?
choices: They should replace medical treatment.
They have serious side effects.
They are a useful addition to treatment but not a cure.
They produce permanent improvements.
questions.explanation: 最終段落に、治療法ではなく効果も一時的だが、安く副作用も少ないので医療の貴重な補完になるとある。

title: The Sharing Economy and Housing
passage:
Home-sharing platforms, which allow people to rent out rooms or entire apartments to travelers, have become extremely popular over the past fifteen years. For travelers, these services often offer cheaper accommodation than hotels and the chance to stay in residential neighborhoods. For homeowners, they provide an extra source of income.

However, many cities have begun to worry about the effects of short-term rentals on housing. In popular tourist destinations, some property owners have discovered that they can earn more by renting apartments to tourists than to long-term residents. As a result, fewer homes are available for local people, and rents have risen. In some historic city centers, residents complain that their neighborhoods have lost their sense of community, as apartments are filled with constantly changing groups of visitors.

In response, several cities have introduced regulations. Amsterdam limits the number of nights per year that an entire home can be rented to tourists, while Barcelona has stopped issuing new licenses for tourist apartments in its city center. New York requires most hosts to be present in the home during guests' stays. Such rules have reduced the number of listings in these cities, although enforcing them can be difficult.

The home-sharing companies argue that they are being unfairly blamed for housing problems that have many causes, including a lack of new construction. They point out that many hosts are ordinary people who depend on the extra income. Most experts agree that short-term rentals are only one factor in rising housing costs, but they say the effect can be significant in neighborhoods popular with tourists.
translation:
旅行者に部屋や家全体を貸し出せる民泊サービスは、この15年で非常に人気になった。旅行者にとっては、ホテルより安く泊まれ、住宅街に滞在できることが多い。家の所有者にとっては、副収入になる。

しかし多くの都市が、短期の貸し出しが住宅に与える影響を心配し始めている。人気の観光地では、長期の住民に貸すより観光客に貸す方が稼げることに気づいた所有者もいる。その結果、地元の人が住める家が減り、家賃が上がった。歴史ある市の中心部では、部屋が入れ替わり立ち替わり訪れる観光客で埋まり、地域のつながりが失われたと住民が訴えている。

これを受けて、規制を導入した都市もある。アムステルダムは家全体を観光客に貸せる日数を年間で制限し、バルセロナは中心部で観光客向けアパートの新規許可の発行をやめた。ニューヨークは、ほとんどの貸し手に宿泊客の滞在中は家にいることを義務づけている。こうした規則でこれらの都市の掲載件数は減ったが、取り締まりは難しい場合がある。

民泊企業は、新築の不足など多くの原因がある住宅問題について、不当に責任を押しつけられていると主張する。貸し手の多くは副収入に頼る普通の人々だと指摘する。ほとんどの専門家は、短期の貸し出しは住宅費上昇の要因の一つにすぎないとしつつ、観光客に人気の地区ではその影響が大きくなりうると言っている。

questions.question: Why have rents risen in some tourist destinations?
choices: Too many new apartments have been built.
Tourists have stopped visiting these cities.
Hotels have become more expensive.
Owners rent homes to tourists instead of local residents.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、観光客に貸す方が稼げるため地元の人が住める家が減り、家賃が上がったとある。

questions.question: What rule has New York introduced?
choices: Tourist apartments are banned in the city center.
Homes can be rented for only a few nights a year.
Most hosts must stay in the home while guests are there.
Hosts must pay a special tourist tax.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、ニューヨークは貸し手に滞在中の在宅を義務づけているとある。日数制限はアムステルダム、新規許可停止はバルセロナ。

questions.question: What do most experts believe?
choices: Home-sharing is the only cause of rising rents.
Short-term rentals are one of several causes of higher housing costs.
Short-term rentals have no effect on housing.
All cities should ban home-sharing completely.
questions.explanation: 最終段落に、短期の貸し出しは要因の一つにすぎないが、観光地では影響が大きくなりうるとある。

title: The Value of Failure in Science
passage:
In popular accounts of science, discoveries often appear to happen in moments of sudden inspiration. In reality, most research involves many experiments that do not work. Scientists spend years testing ideas, and the majority of their hypotheses turn out to be wrong. Some researchers argue that these failures are not a waste of time but an essential part of the scientific process.

One problem is that failed experiments are rarely published. Scientific journals tend to prefer studies with positive, exciting results, a tendency known as publication bias. As a result, other scientists may not know that a particular approach has already been tried and failed, and they may waste time and money repeating the same experiments. Publication bias can also give a misleading picture of how effective a treatment or method really is.

To address this problem, some journals now publish studies regardless of their results, as long as the research methods are sound. In a system called registered reports, scientists submit their research plans before conducting experiments. If the plan is accepted, the journal agrees to publish the study whatever the outcome. Supporters say this encourages careful research design and reduces the pressure to produce dramatic findings.

Failure has also led to some important discoveries by accident. Penicillin, the first widely used antibiotic, was discovered when Alexander Fleming noticed that mold had contaminated one of his experiments and killed the bacteria around it. Such stories remind us that unexpected results, even when they appear to be mistakes, can sometimes open new paths of research.
translation:
一般向けの科学の話では、発見はひらめきの瞬間に起きるように描かれることが多い。実際には、研究のほとんどはうまくいかない多くの実験から成る。科学者は何年もかけて考えを検証し、仮説の大半は誤りだとわかる。こうした失敗は時間の無駄ではなく、科学の過程に欠かせない部分だと主張する研究者もいる。

問題の一つは、失敗した実験がめったに発表されないことだ。科学誌は肯定的で目を引く結果の研究を好む傾向があり、これは出版バイアスと呼ばれる。その結果、他の科学者はある方法がすでに試されて失敗したことを知らず、同じ実験を繰り返して時間とお金を無駄にするかもしれない。出版バイアスは、治療法や手法が実際にどれほど効果的かについて誤った印象を与えることもある。

この問題に対処するため、研究方法が適切であれば結果にかかわらず研究を掲載する学術誌も出てきた。「事前登録報告」と呼ばれる制度では、科学者は実験を行う前に研究計画を提出する。計画が認められれば、学術誌は結果がどうであれ掲載することに同意する。支持者は、これにより研究の設計が丁寧になり、劇的な結果を出さなければという重圧が減ると言う。

失敗が偶然重要な発見につながったこともある。最初に広く使われた抗生物質ペニシリンは、アレクサンダー・フレミングが実験の一つにカビが混入し、その周りの細菌が死んでいることに気づいたことで発見された。こうした話は、予想外の結果は、たとえ間違いに見えても、新しい研究の道を開くことがあると教えてくれる。

questions.question: What is one effect of publication bias?
choices: Journals publish too many negative results.
Research becomes less expensive.
Scientists may repeat experiments that have already failed.
Scientists stop testing new ideas.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、失敗が発表されないため、他の科学者が同じ実験を繰り返して時間とお金を無駄にするかもしれないとある。

questions.question: How do registered reports work?
choices: Scientists publish only their positive results.
Journals agree to publish a study based on its plan, regardless of results.
Experiments are registered after they succeed.
Journals reject all studies with negative results.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、実験前に計画を提出し、認められれば結果にかかわらず掲載されるとある。

questions.question: Why does the author mention the discovery of penicillin?
choices: To explain how antibiotics are tested today
To argue that mistakes should be avoided
To show that an unexpected result can lead to an important discovery
To criticize Alexander Fleming's methods
questions.explanation: 最終段落で、実験の失敗のように見えた出来事が重要な発見につながった例として挙げている。

title: The Four-Day Workweek in Practice
passage:
In recent years, an increasing number of companies have tested a four-day workweek, in which employees work fewer hours without a cut in pay. The idea is based on the belief that people can achieve the same results in less time if they are well rested and motivated. One of the largest trials was conducted in the United Kingdom in 2022, involving about 60 companies and nearly 3,000 employees.

The results were largely positive. Most companies reported that productivity and revenue stayed the same or increased during the six-month trial. Employees said they felt less stressed and had more time for family and hobbies, and the number of sick days fell. After the trial, the majority of the participating companies decided to continue with the shorter week.

However, critics point out several limitations. The companies that joined the trial did so voluntarily, so they may have been especially suited to the change. Many were small businesses in fields such as marketing and technology, where work can be organized flexibly. It is less clear how a four-day week would work in industries such as healthcare, manufacturing, or retail, where staff must be present at fixed times.

To make the shorter week work, many companies changed the way they operated. They reduced the number and length of meetings, set times when employees could work without interruptions, and used technology to automate routine tasks. Some experts suggest that these changes, rather than the extra day off itself, may be the main reason for the improvements in productivity. If so, even companies that keep a five-day week might benefit from adopting similar practices.
translation:
近年、給料を減らさずに労働時間を短くする週4日勤務を試す企業が増えている。この考えは、十分に休んで意欲のある人は、より短い時間で同じ成果を出せるという考えに基づく。最大規模の試験の一つは2022年に英国で行われ、約60社と約3,000人の従業員が参加した。

結果はおおむね良好だった。ほとんどの企業が、6か月の試験期間中、生産性と収益は変わらないか増えたと報告した。従業員はストレスが減り、家族や趣味の時間が増えたと答え、病欠の日数も減った。試験後、参加企業の大半が短い週を続けることにした。

しかし批判する人たちはいくつかの限界を指摘する。試験に参加した企業は自ら手を挙げたので、変化に特に向いていた可能性がある。多くはマーケティングやテクノロジーなど、仕事を柔軟に組める分野の小規模企業だった。医療、製造、小売など、決まった時間にスタッフがいなければならない業界で週4日制がどう機能するかは、あまりはっきりしない。

短い週をうまく機能させるため、多くの企業は仕事のやり方を変えた。会議の数と長さを減らし、邪魔されずに働ける時間を設け、定型作業を技術で自動化した。生産性が上がった主な理由は、休みが1日増えたことそのものより、こうした変化だったのではないかと考える専門家もいる。そうだとすれば、週5日制を続ける企業でも、同じような取り組みを取り入れれば恩恵を受けられるかもしれない。

questions.question: What happened after the trial in the United Kingdom?
choices: Most companies chose to keep the four-day week.
Most companies returned to a five-day week.
Employees asked to work longer hours.
The government made the four-day week illegal.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、試験後、参加企業の大半が短い週を続けることにしたとある。

questions.question: What is one limitation of the trial pointed out by critics?
choices: The companies may have been especially suitable for the change.
The trial lasted only one week.
Only hospitals took part.
Employees' pay was reduced.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、自ら手を挙げた企業なので変化に特に向いていた可能性があると指摘されている。

questions.question: What do some experts suggest in the final paragraph?
choices: An extra day off is the only reason for higher productivity.
Companies should hold more meetings.
Changes in work practices may explain much of the productivity gain.
Five-day weeks are always less productive.
questions.explanation: 会議の削減などの変化こそが生産性向上の主な理由かもしれないと述べている。

title: Saving Water in Agriculture
passage:
Agriculture accounts for about 70 percent of the fresh water used by humans worldwide. As populations grow and climate change makes droughts more frequent, many regions are facing serious water shortages. Finding ways to grow food with less water has therefore become one of the most important challenges of the century.

Traditional irrigation methods are often inefficient. In flood irrigation, for example, farmers cover entire fields with water, and much of it evaporates or soaks into the ground beyond the reach of plant roots. Drip irrigation, by contrast, delivers small amounts of water directly to the roots through tubes. Studies have shown that it can reduce water use by 30 to 50 percent while maintaining or even increasing crop yields.

Despite these benefits, drip irrigation has not been widely adopted in many developing countries. The equipment is expensive to install, and farmers need training to use and maintain it. Some governments now offer subsidies to help small farmers buy drip systems. In India, for example, such programs have helped hundreds of thousands of farmers switch to more efficient methods.

Technology is also offering new solutions. Sensors placed in the soil can measure moisture levels and send information to farmers' smartphones, allowing them to water crops only when necessary. Scientists are also developing crop varieties that can survive with less water. However, experts warn that saving water on farms may not reduce total water use if farmers simply use the savings to expand their fields. They argue that efficient technology must be combined with policies that limit how much water can be taken from rivers and underground sources.
translation:
世界で人間が使う淡水の約70%を農業が占めている。人口が増え、気候変動で干ばつが頻繁になる中、多くの地域が深刻な水不足に直面している。そのため、少ない水で食料を育てる方法を見つけることは、今世紀の最も重要な課題の一つになった。

従来のかんがい方法は非効率なことが多い。たとえば湛水かんがいでは、畑全体を水で覆うので、多くの水が蒸発したり、根の届かない地中にしみこんだりする。一方、点滴かんがいは管を通して少量の水を直接根に届ける。研究によれば、収穫量を保つか増やしながら、水の使用量を30〜50%減らせる。

こうした利点があるにもかかわらず、多くの途上国では点滴かんがいはあまり普及していない。設備の設置費用が高く、使い方や手入れの訓練も必要だ。小規模農家が点滴かんがいの設備を買えるよう補助金を出す政府も出てきた。たとえばインドでは、こうした制度で何十万もの農家がより効率的な方法に切り替えた。

技術も新しい解決策をもたらしている。土に埋めたセンサーが水分量を測って農家のスマートフォンに知らせ、必要なときだけ水をやれるようにする。科学者は、少ない水でも育つ作物の品種も開発している。しかし専門家は、農家が節約した水で畑を広げるだけなら、農場で水を節約しても全体の使用量は減らないかもしれないと警告する。効率的な技術は、川や地下水から取水できる量を制限する政策と組み合わせなければならないと彼らは主張する。

questions.question: What is an advantage of drip irrigation?
choices: It covers entire fields with water.
It uses much less water without lowering crop yields.
It requires no equipment.
It is cheaper to install than other methods.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、収穫量を保つか増やしながら水を30〜50%減らせるとある。設置費用は高い(第3段落)。

questions.question: Why has drip irrigation not spread widely in many developing countries?
choices: Farmers do not need to save water.
Its equipment is costly and requires training to use.
It reduces crop yields.
Governments have banned it.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、設置費用が高く訓練も必要だとある。

questions.question: What warning do experts give in the final paragraph?
choices: Soil sensors are too inaccurate to be useful.
Water savings may be used to expand farming rather than reduce total use.
New crop varieties need more water.
Smartphones are not available to farmers.
questions.explanation: 節約した水で畑を広げれば全体の使用量は減らないかもしれないと警告している。

title: The Psychology of Online Reviews
passage:
Before buying a product, booking a hotel, or choosing a restaurant, many people now read online reviews. Surveys suggest that most consumers trust these reviews almost as much as personal recommendations from friends. However, research shows that online reviews do not always give an accurate picture of quality.

One reason is that the people who write reviews are not typical customers. Those who have very positive or very negative experiences are much more likely to leave a review than those whose experience was average. As a result, ratings for many products tend to cluster at the extremes, with large numbers of five-star and one-star reviews and relatively few in between.

Another problem is the influence of earlier reviews. In one experiment, researchers randomly gave some comments on a website an extra positive vote. Later visitors were significantly more likely to give these comments positive votes too, creating a lasting effect. This suggests that early reviews can shape how later customers evaluate a product, regardless of its actual quality. In addition, some businesses have been caught paying for fake positive reviews or posting negative reviews of their competitors.

Experts recommend several strategies for using reviews wisely. Rather than focusing on the average rating, readers should look at the content of detailed reviews and pay attention to problems that are mentioned repeatedly. Reviews that describe specific experiences are generally more reliable than short ones that simply praise or criticize. Finally, readers should be cautious about products with a small number of reviews, since a few opinions can easily give a misleading impression.
translation:
商品を買う前、ホテルを予約する前、レストランを選ぶ前に、今では多くの人がネットの口コミを読む。調査によれば、ほとんどの消費者は口コミを、友人からの個人的なおすすめとほぼ同じくらい信頼している。しかし研究によると、ネットの口コミが常に質を正確に示しているわけではない。

理由の一つは、口コミを書く人が典型的な客ではないことだ。非常に良い、または非常に悪い経験をした人は、平凡な経験をした人よりはるかに口コミを残しやすい。その結果、多くの商品の評価は両極端に偏り、星5つと星1つが多く、中間は比較的少なくなる。

もう一つの問題は、先に書かれた口コミの影響だ。ある実験では、研究者がウェブサイト上のいくつかのコメントに、無作為に好意的な票を1つ追加した。後から訪れた人は、こうしたコメントにも好意的な票を入れる傾向がかなり強く、影響が長く続いた。これは、実際の質にかかわらず、初期の口コミが後の客の評価を左右しうることを示している。さらに、好意的な偽の口コミにお金を払ったり、競合他社の悪い口コミを投稿したりしていたことが発覚した企業もある。

専門家は、口コミを賢く使うためのいくつかの方法を勧めている。平均評価に注目するより、詳しい口コミの内容を読み、繰り返し挙げられている問題に注意すべきだ。具体的な経験を書いた口コミは、単に褒めたり批判したりする短い口コミより、一般に信頼できる。最後に、口コミの数が少ない商品には注意すべきだ。少数の意見は簡単に誤った印象を与えるからだ。

questions.question: Why do ratings for many products tend to be extremely high or low?
choices: People with very good or very bad experiences are more likely to write reviews.
Most customers have average experiences and write long reviews.
Websites delete all neutral reviews.
Companies require customers to give five stars.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、非常に良い・悪い経験をした人の方が口コミを書きやすいので両極端に偏るとある。

questions.question: What did the experiment with extra positive votes show?
choices: Early ratings can influence later customers' opinions.
Later visitors ignored earlier votes.
Positive votes made comments less popular.
Fake reviews are easy to identify.
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、追加の好意的な票が後の訪問者の評価にも影響し、長く続いたとある。

questions.question: What do experts recommend?
choices: Choosing products with the highest average rating
Trusting products with only a few reviews
Ignoring all negative reviews
Reading detailed reviews and looking for repeated problems
questions.explanation: 最終段落に、平均評価より詳しい口コミの内容を読み、繰り返し挙げられる問題に注意するよう勧めている。

title: Rebuilding Forests After Wildfires
passage:
Wildfires have become larger and more frequent in many parts of the world, including the western United States, Australia, and southern Europe. Rising temperatures and longer dry seasons have made forests more vulnerable, and fires that once occurred every few decades now return within a few years. After a major fire, governments often face pressure to replant trees as quickly as possible.

However, some ecologists warn that replanting is not always the best approach. Many forests have evolved alongside fire and can recover naturally. Some tree species even depend on fire: certain pine trees have cones that open only when exposed to high temperatures, releasing seeds onto the newly cleared ground. In such forests, planting trees by hand may be unnecessary and can even interfere with natural recovery.

In other cases, however, natural recovery may not be possible. When fires are extremely intense, they can destroy all the seeds in the soil and kill the trees that would normally provide new seeds. If fires return before young trees have grown large enough to produce seeds, forests may be replaced by grasslands or shrubs. In these situations, scientists say that careful replanting can play an important role.

Researchers are also rethinking which trees to plant. In the past, foresters often replanted large areas with a single species that grew quickly and had commercial value. Such forests, however, can be especially vulnerable to fire and disease. Many experts now recommend planting a mix of native species that are better suited to future climate conditions, and spacing trees more widely so that fires are less likely to spread rapidly.
translation:
米国西部、オーストラリア、南ヨーロッパなど、世界の多くの地域で山火事が大規模化し、頻発するようになった。気温の上昇と乾季の長期化で森は燃えやすくなり、かつて数十年に一度だった火事が、今では数年のうちに再び起きる。大きな火事の後、政府はできるだけ早く木を植え直すよう求められることが多い。

しかし一部の生態学者は、植え直しが常に最善とは限らないと警告する。多くの森は火とともに進化し、自然に回復できる。火に頼る樹種さえある。ある種のマツは、高温にさらされたときだけ開く松かさを持ち、焼けて開けた地面に種を落とす。こうした森では、人の手で植えることは不要で、自然の回復を妨げることさえある。

しかし、自然の回復が不可能な場合もある。火事が極めて激しいと、土の中の種がすべて焼け、ふつうなら新しい種を落とす木も死んでしまう。若木が種をつけるほど育つ前に再び火事が起きると、森が草地や低木の茂みに変わってしまうこともある。こうした場合には、慎重な植え直しが重要な役割を果たしうると科学者は言う。

研究者たちは、どの木を植えるかも考え直している。かつて林業家は、成長が速く商業的価値のある単一の種を広い範囲に植えることが多かった。しかしそうした森は、火事や病気に特に弱いことがある。今では多くの専門家が、将来の気候に適した在来種を混ぜて植え、火が急速に広がりにくいよう木の間隔を広くとることを勧めている。

questions.question: Why do some ecologists say replanting is not always necessary?
choices: Trees cannot grow after a wildfire.
Replanting is too expensive for governments.
Many forests can recover naturally after fire.
Wildfires are becoming less frequent.
questions.explanation: 第2段落に、多くの森は火とともに進化し自然に回復できるとある。

questions.question: In what situation do scientists say replanting can be important?
choices: When forests have many pine trees
When fires occur only once every few decades
When trees produce large numbers of seeds
When fires are so intense that natural recovery is not possible
questions.explanation: 第3段落に、火事が激しく種が失われ自然回復が不可能な場合、植え直しが重要な役割を果たしうるとある。

questions.question: What do many experts now recommend?
choices: Planting a single fast-growing species
Planting trees as close together as possible
Avoiding native species
Planting a variety of native species with more space between trees
questions.explanation: 最終段落に、在来種を混ぜて植え、木の間隔を広くとることを勧めているとある。
